correctness.rationale: Multiplying by e^{2lambda tau} factors the characteristic equation through y=lambda e^{lambda tau}, where y solves y^2+Py+Q=0. For real negative roots, the first imaginary crossing is generated by the root of largest magnitude and occurs at pi/(2|y|), giving the first branch. For conjugate roots, both have modulus sqrt(Q) and the phase condition gives the second branch. Differentiating lambda e^{lambda tau}=y gives d lambda/d tau=-lambda^2/(1+lambda tau), whose real part at a simple imaginary root is positive. Fresh independent numerical checks on both discriminant regimes and the repeated boundary reproduced zero characteristic residuals and positive crossing direction.
residual_risks: At Delta=0 the critical root is algebraically multiple, so no simple Hopf conclusion follows.

final_claim: For the common-delay coexistence linearization lambda^2+P lambda e^{-lambda tau}+Qe^{-2lambda tau}=0 with zero-delay stability, the exact first stability-loss delay is pi/(P+sqrt(P^2-4Q)) when P^2>=4Q and arcsin(P/(2sqrt(Q)))/sqrt(Q) when P^2<4Q; stability holds exactly before that delay and every simple crossing is left-to-right.
